name: Beaver City Transit
note: City of Beaver + 10-mile radius in Beaver County panhandle

name: Cherokee Strip Transit
note: Alfalfa, Blaine, Grant, Kingfisher, Noble counties fully; portions of Garfield and Kay counties (north-central including Ponca City, Blackwell, Cherokee, Tonkawa, Waukomis, Enid area)

name: Cimarron Public Transit System
note: Service area described as 'Logan County area (Guthrie)'; ODOT Section 5311 provider based in Guthrie. County boundary used as approximate proxy since exact coverage within county not specified.

name: Delta Public Transit
note: McClain and Garvin counties fully; southern Cleveland County only

name: Enid Public Transportation Authority (EPTA)
note: Curb-to-curb service within Enid city limits, Garfield County

name: Guymon Transit - The Ride
note: Service area described as 'Guymon / Texas County, Oklahoma panhandle'; City of Guymon service with broader Texas County panhandle coverage implied. County boundary used as approximate proxy since exact coverage within county not specified.

name: JAMM Transit
note: Covers Johnston, Atoka, Marshall, and Murray counties in southeastern Oklahoma

name: KI BOIS Area Transit System (KATS)
note: Multi-county service based in Stigler; official site lists differ; coverage includes Haskell, Latimer, Le Flore, McIntosh, Pittsburg, Sequoyah and potentially others (Adair, Cherokee, Hughes, Okfuskee, Okmulgee, Wagoner); exact boundaries not confirmed

name: Little Dixie Transit
note: Southeastern Oklahoma: McCurtain, Choctaw, and Pushmataha counties (corrected from initial 5-county list; Atoka and Bryan not verified by sources)

name: MTTA On-Demand Microtransit (GoPass App)
note: Only the Broken Arrow zone (20 sq mi, launched Feb 2024) is drawn, as a circle of that size clipped to Broken Arrow city limits; MetroLink Tulsa's other GoPass on-demand zones in the Tulsa metro are not mapped (zone maps needed).

name: Norman On-Demand
note: City of Norman; serves evening/late-night and Sunday zones

name: Pelivan Transit
note: Northeastern Oklahoma: Craig, Delaware, Mayes, Nowata, Ottawa, and Rogers counties including Owasso/Collinsville zone

name: PICK Transportation
note: SUMC case study names all 21 launch/expansion communities served by the Pelivan-led consortium (Atoka, Bartlesville, Owasso, Tahlequah plus 17 added communities). Service area has continued to evolve since (e.g. Altus added 2025, per a later SUMC update), so this list reflects the documented 21-community footprint rather than the current live roster. https://learn.sharedusemobilitycenter.org/overview/rural-agencies-launch-mobility-on-demand-pilot-21-counties-ok-2021/

name: Red River Public Transportation Service
note: 16 counties explicitly listed in Region/Service Area

name: Southern Oklahoma Rural Transportation System
note: Centered in Ardmore (Carter County); exact county coverage unverified

name: Southwest Transit
note: ODOT S5311 profile identifies service as Jackson, Harmon and Greer counties (demand-response, general public); hub cities Altus, Hollis, Mangum, Granite. https://oklahoma.gov/odot/programs-and-projects/programs/multimodal/transit-programs/section-5311-rural/southwest-transit.html
